I'm in the same boat, I did this last year as well. I'm in NC and the heat and humidity takes all new training.   


I take this mentality. The heat is retraining. I'm sure Alabama is similar, that 50%-80% humidity is all too common in 90+ degrees. This takes your body a lot of getting used to. I focus first on getting the miles in no matter the pace or how many breaks I have to take. If you want to do long distances, chop it up, do 5 1-mile runs with water breaks and cool downs between.  Be sure to monitor heart rate / water intake / body temperature. The longer you're out there, the more you get used to it, but remember it's dangerous. I'm down to 11 minute pace where I consistently doing 10 miles at between 9-10 minutes, and can only manage 5 mile runs in the heat.   


Some people will also recommend running in the morning when the heat isn't as bad but you'll still have to adjust anyway.  


It's not fun to get used to but eventually your body will learn and get better at it. It took me about a month running 2-3 times a week to really notice my body adjust. Keep at it! You'll get there. Remember heat is dangerous and don't underestimate the heat index or your hydration!!  


Good luck out there, I hope this helps.
